ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS
January 202 4
DOB ISSUES MONTHLY ENFORCEMENT BULLETIN
Report Highlights DOB Enforcement Outcomes from January 2024 to Deter
Bad Actors and Keep New Yorkers Safe
New York, NY – The New York City Department of Buildings released its enforcement
bulletin for January 2024, which provides highlights of the agency’s actions to sanction
and deter bad actors in the construction industry through the enforcement of safety laws
and codes of conduct. Today’s bulletin includes summaries of DOB-imposed
disciplinary actions, including penalties, license suspensions and revocations.
The actions below represent a portion of DOB’s overall work to enforce the City’s
building codes and safety laws, in addition to the thousands of inspections conducted
and violations issued by the agency each month for illegal building and construction
conditions.
DOB completed several major enforcement actions in January, including:
• 10 violations and $175,000 in penalties issued for Failure to Safeguard
construction sites at 10 locations.
• 6 violations and $29,125 in penalties, including daily penalties, issued for illegal
building alterations at x locations.
• 4 violations and $40,000 in penalties issued to 4 individuals for failure to carry out
the duties of a construction superintendent.
Below are individual enforcement highlights for January 2024:
Bronx
• $206,400 in total penalties issued to Bamms Realty III, LLC for violations
recorded at 921 East 149th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for the
illegal outdoor advertising sign which violated the Zoning Resolution height and
surface area restrictions. The Respondent was also cited for failure to comply
with the Commissioner’s Orders to file certificates of corrections for previous
violations, which began in June 2021.

• $15,000 in penalties issued to Triton Construction Co for violations recorded at
1010 Lincoln Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations after a worker without an
SST card was using a ladder to install cable in a 10-foot-high ceiling and was
found on floor; worker had not been given pre-shift training or site safety
orientation.
• $12,500 in penalties issued to Lemle & Wolf Construction Corp for violations
recorded at 472 Willis Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to
institute safety measures after plumbers on 13th floor of a construction site
dislodged debris that fell on worker below at 6th floor, and failed to remove debris.
• $7,500 in total penalties issued to Zefi & Co LLC for violations recorded at 1550
White Plains Road. DOB inspectors issued violations after a worker fell from a
scaffold and that was not built to Code, and no report was made to DOB.
• $6,250 in penalties issued to 10 Clay Properties LLC for violations recorded at
1046 Clay Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to maintain
building after a decorative stone above first floor window dislodged and fell to
ground, knocking a window awning off.
• $2,500 in penalties issued to Abdul Gul for violations recorded at 900 Grand
Concourse. DOB inspectors issued violations for the suspended scaffold which
had inadequate tie lines and inadequate anchor points.
• A signed stipulation agreement was signed by the owners of 1927 Gildersleeve
Avenue to discontinue commercial vehicle and other junk storage in a residential
district.

Brooklyn
• $25,000 in penalties issued to MJM Associates Construction LLC for violations
recorded at 345 Avenue U. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to
safeguard after finding concrete droppings on the adjacent property’s windows,
doors, and front steps.
• $10,000 in penalties issued to Gabriel Krochmal for violations recorded at 1252
Herkimer Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to file a tenant
protection plan after finding
• $7,200 in penalties issued to BG Flatlands LLC for violations recorded at 12091
Flatlands Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations for unlicensed electrical
work and unsafe electrical equipment.
• $5,000 in penalties issued to ZJW Construction Inc. for violations recorded at 550
55th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to institute safety
measures after finding a 5’ x 7’ hole in ground floor apartment leading to
basement with no guardrails.
• $5,000 in penalties issued to JRM Development LLC for violations recorded at
2777 Atlantic Ave. DOB inspectors issued violations for insufficient stairs and
ladders at a building under construction, as well as a blocked sidewalk that
forced pedestrians into street.
• $2,500 in penalties issued to Ninth Avenue Construction GR for violations
recorded at 90 Wharf Drive. DOB inspectors issued violations for Failure to
comply with manufacturer’s specifications after worker fell off 8-foot A-frame
ladder while sealing glass at first floor level of 40 story building.

• $2,500 in penalties issued to Aryeh Nosson Breier for violations recorded at 1542
38th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for work without a permit after
finding unpermitted demolition work.
• $1,250 in penalties issued to Eli Y. Reifer for violations recorded at 5101 17th
Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations for work without a permit after finding
an unpermitted extension built at the premises.
Manhattan
• $32,500 in penalties issued to Urban Atelier Group LLC for violations recorded at
270 West 96th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard
after a wooden spool rolled off truck and down the street during delivery of
electrical material, damaging two vehicles. Additional violations for information
not being transmitted during toolbox talks, work not conforming to plans, and for
materials that were to be received “on site” being received in the street.
• $25,000in penalties issued to Rockefeller University for violations recorded at
1198 York Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations after item previously filed in
a Safe With Repair and Maintenance Program (SWARMP) report were not
corrected and a sidewalk shed was not in place.
• $18,750 in penalties issued to 147 West 24th Street LLC for violations recorded at
147 West 24 Street. DOB inspectors issued violations after finding extensive
work without a permit across the 7-story building.
• $17,500 in penalties issued to Abeco Construction LLC for violations recorded at
430 West Broadway. DOB inspectors issued violations after a fire occurred at a
demolition site from hot welding operation with no fire guards or site safety
orientation for workers.
• $12,500 in penalties issued to Triton Construction LLC for violations recorded at
1245 Broadway. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to comply with
manufacturer’s specifications after a worker fell from a baker’s scaffold that was
being used without attaching outriggers while doing framing.
• $10,000 in penalties issued to Prat Enterprises Corp. for violations recorded at
185 West End Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations after a loose brick fell
from scaffold and struck a parked car. Worker on site received no site safety
orientation, and incident was not reported immediately.
• $5,000 in penalties issued to Front Wave Construction for violations recorded at
59 Henry Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard after a
clogged hose burst during concrete pour, striking worker in the face. Inspectors
observed no competent person on site who was able to stop the pour.
• $1,250 in penalties issued to Javind Apartment Charles Coutinho LLC for
violations recorded at 32 West 86th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for
failure to maintain elevator after an elevator was found to be inoperable.

Queens
• $7,500 in penalties issued to Zefi & Co LLC for violations recorded at 1550 White
Plains Road. DOB inspectors issued violations after worker fell from scaffold that
was not Code compliant and no report was made to DOB.
• $2,500 in penalties issued to Stonehill Construction Services for violations
recorded at 83-05 116th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for improper
concrete washout after observing washout to be allowed to leach into the ground.
• A signed stipulation agreement was signed by the owners of 60-32 78th Avenue
to discontinue automobile repairs in a residential district.
• A 2017 closure order at 149-45 24 Avenue due to commercial vehicle storage,
junk salvage storage and a contractor’s yard, was rescinded by DOB after the
property owner removed the illegal conditions from the lot.

Construction and Design Professionals
• DOB’s Special Enforcement Team (SET) audited 9 professionally certified
applications submitted by Registered Architect Adam Snyder and found major
code non-compliances, including filing Alteration Type 2 applications despite
proposing changes in use, egress, and/or occupancy, which require Alteration
Type 1 applications for a new or amended Certificate of Occupancy; proposing
plans that fail to provide two means of egress; proposing plans that failed to
include a fire rated enclosure for the stairs; proposing plans that include a double
door that obstructs egress; and various other violations of code and rules,
including the Zoning Resolution, Building Code, and Administrative Code. Based
on the audits, SET offered a voluntary surrender of respondent’s Professional
Certification and Directive 14 privileges. Respondent has not signed.
• DOB’s Special Enforcement Team (SET) audited 8 professionally certified
applications submitted by Professional Engineer Dongsheng Lu and found major
code non-compliances, including filing Alteration Type 2 applications despite
proposing changes in use, egress, and/or occupancy, which require Alteration
Type 1 applications for a new or amended Certificate of Occupancy; proposing
plans that are not ADA compliant; proposing plans that fail to provide tenants
with direct access to the required number of exits without passing through parts
of the premises occupied by other tenants; failing to provide fire rating notes; and
various other violations of code and rules, including the Zoning Resolution,
Building Code, and Administrative Code. Based on failed audits, SET offered a
voluntary surrender of Professional Certification and Directive 14 privileges.
Respondent has not signed.
• DOB’s Special Enforcement Team (SET) audited 8 professionally certified
applications submitted by Professional Engineer Mohammad Ahead, including
filing Alteration Type 2 applications despite proposing changes in use, egress,
and/or occupancy, which require Alteration Type 1 applications for a new or
amended Certificate of Occupancy; proposing plans that fail to include a complete
tenant protection plan; proposing plans that fail to identify safety measures to
maintain fire safety; failure to include special inspection items related to structural
stability; and various other violations of code and rules, including the Zoning
Resolution, Building Code, and Administrative Code. Based on the audits, SET
offered a voluntary surrender of Professional Certification and Directive 14
privileges. Respondent has not signed.
• DOB’s Special Enforcement team (SET) filed an amended petition at OATH to
suspend Professional Engineer Richard Koenigsburg’s Qualified Exterior Wall
Inspector (QEWI) privileges after the partial collapse of 1915 Billingsley Terrace in
the Bronx. The Department seeks the suspension based on audits of

Respondent’s Cycle 7, Cycle 8, and Cycle 9 Façade Inspection & Safety Program
(FISP) reports and a separate audit of the façade repair application and plans.
